analysis.title: Shifting sands (Mullaney on the Markets, November 2026)
key_insights: October 2026: cap-weighted S&P 500 fell 0.87% while the equal-weighted S&P 500 gained 5.00%, the largest gap favoring equal weight since April 2009. The Magnificent Seven fell 4.67% and the S&P 493 gained 1.34%. The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.63% on concerns about monetizing the AI buildout.

The Bloomberg US Aggregate Bond Index returned 2.44% in October, its best month since December 2023, as investors sought safety. Year to date it is down 0.54% as inflation has made little progress toward the Fed's 2% target.
Year to date through October: S&P 500 +11.75%, S&P 500 Equal Weight +15.51%, Magnificent 7 +4.08%, S&P 493 +14.56%, Nasdaq 100 +12.98%.

Energy was the top sector in October (+14.00%) as the war in Iran and threats of escalation after the midterms pushed WTI from $88.42 to $104.12 and Brent from $97.66 to $111.73. Q3 EPS rose 104% at ExxonMobil and 277% at Chevron. Energy is +59.92% year to date.
Consumer Staples had its best monthly return since October 2000 (+11.62%), with Utilities (+10.17%) and Health Care (+9.87%) also strong as investors moved to defensive sectors.

Communication Services was the October laggard (-15.11%), as Alphabet (56% of the sector, -18.53%) and Meta (24%, -15.19%) accounted for 94% of the sector loss. AI capex has not visibly lifted their revenues. The sector is last year to date (-11.31%).
Eli Lilly is 15% of the Health Care sector's weight but drove 23% of its year-to-date return (+32.54%), on the GLP-1 franchise.

Value beat growth by an average of 8.16% in October across the three Russell cap ranges, the best month for value versus growth since March 2001. Year-to-date value outperformance averages 20.23%, also the best since 2001.

October was risk-off: low-beta (+10.18% for the lowest quintile versus -1.24% for the highest) and high-quality stocks outperformed, and small caps beat large. The Russell 1000 has 37.1% in Technology versus 13.4% for the Russell 2000. Year to date, risk-on factors still lead: high beta lags, low quality (+15.86%) beats high quality (+9.69%), and small caps edge large.

MSCI EAFE returned -0.72% in USD in October, ahead of the S&P 500 on a cap-weighted basis, while the dollar rose (DXY +0.42%). Emerging markets fell 8.04% in USD, led by South Korea (-15.57%) and Taiwan (-8.37%) on Samsung (-15.00%), SK Hynix (-19.01%) and TSMC (-6.69%).
Brazil fell 12.11% in October after Lula's surprise re-election to a fourth term over Flávio Bolsonaro, who had nearly 80% odds on prediction markets.

Democrats won the House and Senate and nearly all contested governorships in the November 3 midterms. Historically the president's party loses seats in midterms. The president retains executive orders and the veto.
In the 22 years with a Republican president and Democratic House and Senate, the S&P 500 had a positive return 73% of the time, averaging 8.57%.

In every midterm year since 1962 the S&P 500 has had a drawdown, usually followed by a significant rally. After both chambers flipped in 1994 and 2006, stocks were positive a year later and the Nasdaq 100 outperformed the S&P 500.

Implied volatility spiked after the midterms in both the VIX and VXN, and the VXN-VIX gap is at an extreme level. Historically that gap has reverted quickly, and reversion would come from a decline in tech-heavy Nasdaq volatility.

Bloomberg's assessment of a Democratic Congress: significant impact on judges and appointments, moderate on oversight, legislation and appropriations, limited on trade and tariffs, foreign policy and impeachment.

tension_points.bull_case: Stocks were positive one year after both chambers flipped in 1994 and 2006, the S&P 500 has been positive 73% of the time under a Republican president with a Democratic Congress, and Big Tech outperformed the S&P 500 after both flips.
tension_points.bear_case: The S&P 500 has had a drawdown in every midterm year since 1962, and a Democratic Congress can block appointments and gain leverage over appropriations. Volatility spiked after the election.

theme_stances.key_argument: Concerns about monetizing the AI buildout drove a rotation out of megacap tech into the S&P 493, value and defensives.

theme_stances.key_argument: Historically a Democratic Congress under a Republican president has not been an impediment to stock returns, and Big Tech outperformed after prior double flips.
theme_stances.evidence: has not necessarily been an impediment to stock returns
